summary: Pushmataha County, OK metal fire tower on Flagpole Mountain near Clayton; Wikipedia says it stands but is no longer operational. No build date or access found.

facts.design: Metal lattice tower, several stories tall
facts.status_note: No longer operational, according to Wikipedia; the article is undated

evidence.supports: Flagpole Mountain retains a fire tower, built of metal and several stories tall
evidence.quote: Flagpole Mountain retains a fire tower. Built of metal and several stories tall

evidence.supports: the tower was once one of a network of towers, all staffed
evidence.quote: it was once part of a network of towers, all staffed, from which a fire watch was maintained

evidence.supports: the tower is the only one remaining in Pushmataha County and is no longer operational
evidence.quote: It is the only tower remaining in Pushmataha County, although it is no longer operational.

evidence.supports: views from the tower stretch for many miles in any direction
evidence.quote: Views from the tower offer a panorama stretching for many miles in any direction.

evidence.supports: Flagpole Mountain frames Clayton on the west, at 1,562 feet
evidence.quote: Clayton, located in the Kiamichi River valley, is framed on its west by Flagpole Mountain (1,562 ft.)

evidence.supports: OpenStreetMap names the tower Flagpole Lookout Tower
OpenStreetMap tags the construction as lattice

corrections.why: Forest Lookouts prints a bare S after the county with no legend, and no source read names an agency for this tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: OpenStreetMap tags the tower at 562 m. Wikipedia gives Flagpole Mountain as 1,562 ft (about 476 m). These may measure different points, and the sources do not settle it, so the record keeps the OpenStreetMap figure.

notes_for_editor: Wikipedia (Clayton article) is the only source for condition and the only-remaining-tower claim. Its tower sentences are undated and no citation was visible in what we read. A search snippet from the Pushmataha County Historical Society Facebook group says Flagpole is one of two towers remaining in the county, which contradicts Wikipedia's only-tower wording; the page returned only a login stub, so it is not cited. A search snippet from a Facebook photography post says the tower was built in the 1930s during the Roosevelt-era tree army; that page did not load, so no build date is recorded. Staffing 'unstaffed' is inferred from 'no longer operational'. Access and ownership are unknown. Research used 1 web search and about 3 page reads for this tower, plus shared Oklahoma pages.
